sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved funding, not “Avoid — fraud”. Mason has genuinely scaled a Mumbai-region building contractor, but the listed equity now also finances property, associates and a newly consolidated developer. FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹131.32 cr and attributable PAT ₹21.87 cr. The attractive-looking earnings multiple is not an owner-cash return: parent CFO after moving debt additions out of operating cash was −₹40.18 cr in FY26. Prior FY25 was also negative on the same economic basis. These are not explained away by the acquired subsidiary alone. [ar26; ar25]

The constructive case is tangible: owned execution equipment, repeat clients, profitable contracts, a large fresh-equity cushion and an unmodified audit with no reported lender default. The opposing case is equally tangible: capital tied in WIP, aged receivables and development investments; demand loans with interest credited rather than verified collected; and cash-credit/short-tenor facilities with dates before the investment cutoff. A positive terminal spreadsheet cannot settle those interim claims.

BQS and GQS are descriptive quality measures, not investment recommendations. GQS is capped at 5 because multi-year cash realization is persistently weak. IAS is NS rather than a fabricated low or neutral number. The ₹97 quote is authenticated on 19 October, while the analytical investment horizon is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031. Ordinary expected returns and entry prices are withheld until current financeability is demonstrated. Conditional recovery and explicit rescue branches remain useful diagnostics, not buy targets. [market60; security_master]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Mason earns revenue from building construction, principally residential/commercial high-rise work in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. Contract types range from full-labour execution to part-material/full-labour and lock-and-key scopes. Customers include external developers and increasingly investee developers. FY26 contract sales were ₹130.946 cr; property-management services ₹0.20 cr and scrap ₹0.1726 cr are small. Equipment ownership, site engineers, labour coordination, procurement and client certification are the operational inputs. Revenue is recognized by stage of completion with client/consultant certification, making billing, retention, estimates and cash timing central. [ar26 pp 121–123,153; prospectus]

The economic loop is not “order booked equals cash”: receive scope/site/drawings, mobilize people/equipment, pay suppliers/labour, obtain certification, bill, collect and finally release retention. Delayed handover, drawings, monsoon interruptions, material/labour escalation, rework or a cash-stressed developer can stretch that loop. Historical contracts do not universally protect labour escalation. Tender/security deposits also lock cash before revenue starts.

The new developer exposure is a distinct use of capital. Parent noncurrent investments ₹84.04 cr include flats/shops ₹56.36 cr plus subsidiaries/associates/other stakes; parent long-term loans ₹20.95 cr add creditor exposure. Subsidiary/associate revenue had not established a mature developer track record. The model therefore values only Mason’s parent-share claims with recovery haircuts and no speculative developer profit stream. It never adds the same subsidiary’s gross assets, parent loan and full enterprise value together. [ar26 pp 150–152,187–198]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The best supported advantage is execution competence, not monopoly economics. Owned cranes, pumps and formwork reduce scheduling dependence and support repetitive high-rise processes; repeat-client work and completed projects are evidence of capability. However, equipment can be acquired by competitors, client approvals govern billing, and contracts are won project by project. No independently measured share of a narrowly defined market, sustainable price premium, proprietary licence or high switching cost was found. A small contractor’s unusually high reported margin should be tested through cash and project mix before being called a moat. [presentation25; prospectus; ar26]

Economically relevant comparators are Capacit’e Infraprojects for high-rise building EPC, B L Kashyap for private commercial/residential contracting, and Ahluwalia Contracts for diversified building/institutional EPC. FY25 primary reports demonstrate established execution platforms rather than Mason-specific technology: Capacit’e describes a high-rise/public-private order base and Vision 2028 target 16.5–17.5% EBITDA, not FY25 actual; BLK’s order mix was 70% commercial and 17% residential; ACIL reported ₹4,154 cr total income and 8.3% EBITDA margin with a diversified regional/public-private mix. ACIL’s FY25 consolidated primary statements show revenue ₹4,098.6231 cr, PAT ₹202.0813 cr, CFO ₹359.4264 cr and normalized EBITDA excluding other income/JVprofit ₹341.9975 cr (8.344%). Its reported CFO/PAT177.86% contrasts with Mason’s negative debt-adjusted FY25 conversion, but Ind AS, interest classification, scale, mix and working-capital timing differ. Capacit’e’s FY25 consolidated audit is qualified on ₹11.5593 cr receivable recovery; it is not presented as a clean financial-quality standard. These are dated operating/cash benchmarks, not synchronized cutoff valuation multiples. [peer_capacite; peer_bl; peer_acil]

Mason’s lower scale, geographic concentration, mixed labour/material scopes and developing investment portfolio make a simple peer P/E average misleading. The modeled 5–9.5 x terminal EPC EBITDA range is an explicit analytical assumption, not a claimed market quotation. Competitive bidding, working-capital intensity and customer financial health matter more to economic durability than construction-sector TAM or generic urbanization forecasts.

Organic versus acquired: Megastone had nil reported revenue during FY26; group revenue growth is still construction activity rather than acquired sales. Nevertheless, economic independence is not the same as organic accounting:₹3 cr sales to Milestone and future work for Magicmind depend partly on entities Mason funds. Incremental EPC margin from an investee project is not added again as the full developer’s profit. Group eliminates intragroup interest and the attributable portion of unrealized profits.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Growth requires funding labour, materials, WIP, certification lag and retentions. In FY26 parent inventory reached ₹67.46 cr and receivables ₹74.02 cr versus annual revenue ₹131.32 cr; security/tender/retention assets add another ₹11.82 cr. Fresh equity expanded capacity to fund this cycle, but financing availability is not proof of high incremental return. A project can be profitable in accounting terms and still consume owner cash for years. [ar26 pp 138–160]

The stable FY24–26 parent bridge normalizes EBIT as PBT+finance cost−other income and NOPAT at a consistent 25% tax assumption. Reported funding proxy equals equity+reported debt−reported cash, including recent deployment but excluding separate warrant deposits and LC reclassification; the increase is compared with incremental NOPAT. An EPC-exposure proxy also removes nonoperating investments/loans, but FY24’s loan/advance category includes deposits/retention that later moved categories, so its apparent precision is explicitly limited. Neither ratio is sold as a project IRR. The recent realty ramp creates a timing drag, while rising operating working capital provides a separate reason not to extrapolate current ROCE. [ar25; ar26]

Reinvestment runway exists in redevelopment and high-rise construction, but permits, land title, bookings, construction financing, partner capital and completion cash flows are not yet a proven repeatable developer system. AOC1 and associate disclosures show little or no operating activity; no return is credited to Niraj MasonJV without operations. The conservative base assumes no discretionary new developer funding beyond Sabve’s plan;₹0/5/15 cr annual additional deployment is stressed. sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The executive leadership is founder-led, with family involvement in finance. FY26 key-managerial compensation was ₹3.085 cr, material relative to group PAT. Commercial related-party construction and loans are disclosed and not automatically abusive; however, the provider of capital can also be the seller and creditor to a developer, weakening the independence of reported order growth. Demand-loan interest credited at 12% is not evidence of cash recovery. [ar26 pp 129–130,155–158]

NSE’s 18 August caution, disclosed 19 August, concerned XBRL voting showing promoters voting in favour where they were interested. The issuer said no financial/operating impact and undertook to address the concern. The September AGM notice expressly requires related parties to abstain on new RPT resolutions. Proposed mandates include an annual ₹695 cr ceiling for Megastone over FY27–31, far beyond current annual revenue, but these authorizations are neither executed contracts nor funded obligations. The 30 September 2026 voting outcome now confirms resolutions 6–12 passed with promoter votes zero. That verifies later corrective voting rather than leaving noncompliance assumed persistent, and supports GOV5 rather than 4; formal retrospective closure of the August caution is not evidenced. Approval ceilings are not actual commitments. [caution; agm_vote; ar26 pp 15–65]

The company secretary resigned 4 September and independent audit-chair Anuradha Parmar resigned 30 September, citing personal occupancy/preoccupations and no other material reason. Earlier CFO transition and the promoter-relative appointment add oversight concentration; none proves financial wrongdoing. Statutory auditor GadaChheda &Co LLP issued unmodified FY25/FY26 opinions; the secretarial auditor change is separate from statutory audit resignation. Execution earns credit for growing certified construction revenue and repeat work, while a new developer pivot and expanding RPT discretion require stronger cash and minority-protection evidence. sections.text:
Full statutory coverage, not just the opinion page: FY26 parent audit/CARO/IFC PDF121–137 and group audit/IFC162–173; FY25 group 71–79 and parent 105–116 were inspected, including image-only annexures. FY26 auditor reports no loan default, wilful-defaulter status, material fraud or undisputed statutory dues older than 6 months; IFC is adequate and audit trail operative from 1 April 2025 without observed tampering. FY25 audit trail similarly operated from 1 April 2024 and its CARO states bank returns agree with the books. FY26 bank-return differences were described as less than 5%, timing/reconciliation and not material, not as nonexistent. [ar26; ar25]

Keep blemishes proportionate. FY26 CARO details preferential fundraising then says no preferential allotment in the following boilerplate clause. The MSME table appears to place ₹3.3107 cr in an interest-labelled row, while the principal/payables ageing establishes it as MSME balances. These are disclosure-control weaknesses requiring correction, not sufficient evidence to invent ₹3.31 cr penalty interest or allege fraud. Tax demand declined from FY25₹13.90 lakh rectification to FY26₹13.24 lakh TDS-credit dispute. Unmodified no-material-uncertainty reporting is dated, not a cash guarantee through October.

Cash normalization is essential. FY25 CFO appears as ₹7.5146 cr in its annual report,₹10.7914 cr in May 2026 comparisons and ₹4.2376 cr in September’s annual report; noncurrent-asset sign/classification differences explain the movements and all preserve ₹1.4284 cr closing cash. Debt and claims are complete in the funding ledger: parent ₹83.2096 cr includes ₹4.3802 cr current maturities; LC ₹3.9146 cr inside payables is moved to financing once. At ₹97 the dated market capitalization is ₹232.218 cr on 23.94 m shares. Group PAT divided by current shares is~₹9.14 EPS, not reported weighted-basic ₹10.29; no warrant cash is assumed already received beyond the ₹3.10 cr deposit in the accounts. The unconverted 1 m warrants require optional additional ₹9.30 cr at ₹124 and are out of the money at the reference quote. Exercise dilutes ownership; it cannot fund a cash trough months before its receipt. [ar26; security_master; market60]

Valuation uses parent-share SOTP: normalized EPC EBITDA/FCFF plus recovery of parent property/stakes/loans, less parent economic debt and other claims. Group debt ₹95.84 cr and NCI ₹0.049 cr are cross-checks, not extra deductions against parent-share assets. Existing operating equipment, deposits, receivables and WIP are not added to an earnings enterprise value as surplus property. Capitalized new developer funding increases the recovery pool only once, with a haircut. Uncollected loan interest has no forecast cash income. Terminal reserve and growth working capital remain invested. Terminal release of restricted FD/unused eligible proceeds and realization of the NAV book-haircut recovery pool are explicit valuation assumptions, not guaranteed unrestricted cash or promised realizations.

Bear/base/bull assumptions link revenue, margin, receivable days, inventory, vendor finance, capex, interest, taxes, developer recovery and multiples. All ordinary returns/entry prices are NS. Nonrescue branches also remain null after any pre-entry or later floor breach. Funded collection-recovery and fully prefunded rescue examples are explicitly conditional. Reverse expectations require a finite funded bracket and near-zero residual; no terminal multiple is accepted as a solution merely because it is an endpoint. sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The permanent-loss mechanism is a funding-and-recovery mismatch, not necessarily fictitious profit. If certification or developer collections slip, WIP and debt rise before cash arrives. A bank can renew on tighter terms or require repayment; suppliers may stop granting credit; a related developer can demand more equity just as the parent needs liquidity. Selling property/stakes under pressure can recover far less than their book cost, and minority shareholders can be diluted even if the eventual projects are viable. [ar26; prospectus]

The bear model slows revenue, lowers margins, raises receivable days/inventory and reduces supplier funding. It also tests receivable loss, the small tax demand, director debt call and lower recovery/multiple. LC is not double-counted; receivable loss is a cash drag relative to the retained WC target, not also a second impairment deduction in SOTP. Sabve’s ₹1.5 cr plan is included across its payment dates; the target’s historical ₹20.7 cr admitted claims are not imported wholesale as issuer liabilities. All original-holder ownership after rescue is reconciled separately from percentage share expansion. [nclt; sabve_update]

Counterevidence matters: positive audited equity, sustained EPCprofit, equipment, repeat business, recent equity raised and no auditor default finding mean that insolvency is not established. Modelled negative cash is a stress outcome. The thesis is falsified constructively by verified renewal, current cash, sustained collections and developer cash distribution; it is worsened by recurring fresh raises merely to fund operating cash deficits, aged-balance escalation, unexplained RPTterms or a genuine auditor qualification. No weighted expected return blends funded and unfunded cases into a benign average.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A5 x or 10 x outcome requires per-share value, not merely a fivefold company order book. At ₹97, the targets are ₹485 and ₹970 per share at 20 October 2031. Current shares, optional warrants and any rescue shares determine the terminal equity required. Issuing shares to finance growth can increase company earnings while preventing original shareholders from reaching either target. A value bridge that holds shares fixed while assuming unlimited working-capital funding is not valid.

The model includes two deliberately separate tests. Static inversions hold the base rescue case’s margin, multiple, recovery pool, debt and cash fixed and solve required terminal revenue. They are labeled optimistic diagnostics because extra growth would itself demand working capital/capex. Dynamic reverse tests then recompute revenue, growth-driven WC, capex, interest, tax, full interval prefunding, whole-share issuance and terminal ownership for every trial growth rate. Only a funded sign-changing bracket within 0–100% annual growth can produce a solved requirement; otherwise the answer is NM, not the nearest tested endpoint. [model assumptions anchored to ar26]

Operational feasibility still requires enough independent projects, supervisors, labour, machines, certifications, customer cash and capital to fund the expansion. The ₹73.26 cr Magicmind award is not an independent demand guarantee; quoted pipeline and unexecuted contract values do not prove conversion capacity. Even a mathematical solution on a rescue branch would be conditional and highly demanding, not an assessed probability of success. The disclosed results should be read alongside terminal share expansion, cash injected and the remaining project-funding gaps, not as a promotional multibagger target.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Before changing G3 Hold, obtain a dated facility bridge: the amount of February WCDL, its actual repayment/rollover date,15 June cash-credit renewal, current sanctioned/drawn/undrawn amounts, covenants/security, current bank cash after restrictions, and next 12 months obligations. Verify with issuer/exchange/lender evidence rather than interpreting a new share price as evidence of financing. Match Sabve CIRP/T+270 payments and closure announcement to the ₹1.5 cr total; do not assume that September share-allotment approval closed the plan. [ar26; nclt; sabve_update]

At the next results, compare collections against the FY26₹74.02 cr receivables and ₹5.79 cr retentions, focusing on ₹11.68 cr over 1 year and the disputed ₹0.78 cr. Track inventory/WIP relative to certified work, cash interest actually received on demand loans, and CFO after removing financing reclassifications. A reduction from recoverable cash is positive; a write-off or recategorization is not the same improvement. Follow maturity extension, fresh equity, related-party balances and capex together, rather than celebrating revenue alone.

For governance, check RPT voting exclusions after the NSEcaution, replacement of the company secretary/audit chair, actual use of the large approval mandates, and the auditor’s correction of preferential/MSME boilerplate. For demand, maintain a tax-normalized remaining-backlog bridge bycustomer, opening orders, additions, executed sales, cancellations and site-readiness. For tradability, resolve the missing 2 September row and verify current spread/depth/restrictions before any actual position decision. Re-score only changed evidence; retain previous raw values and explain every change.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold — unresolved funding and current cash bridge; mixed/limited business quality, not an evidence-backed compounder candidate. The company has grown, but durable owner-cash compounding has not been established. Permanent-impairment risk is High because refinancing, recoverability and dilution can fail together despite profitable accounts. No current recommendation, buy band or executable allocation is inferred from this research. The ₹5 lakh reference is only a consistent liquidity test, not a statement of suitability for a particular investor.

At ₹97 the 500 share lot costs ₹48,500. A budget-constrained floor position is 5,000 shares/₹4,85,000;5,500 shares/₹5,33,500 exceeds the reference budget and is separately shown. Observed 59-session turnover is not the full 60-session measure. At 5% of the conservative observed median thecontinuous theoretical capacity is about 6.7 days for the floor position, but whole-lot rounding gives one lot/day and 10 sessions; at 2% no full lot fits the median-day participation limit. Circuits, spread and lack of buyers may make actual execution worse. [market60; security_master]

A constructive change requires demonstrated financeability without assumed rescue, cash collection rather than reclassification, a clearer attributable return on developer capital, and minority-protection follow-through. If those become available, recompute rather than simply lifting the hold: current debt, sharecount, capital commitments, net recoveries and market price may have changed. A verified collections/renewal recovery can support conditional upside; a funded rescue can preserve the company while still offering insufficient original-holder return. Keeping these branches separate is more useful than declaring every weak score “expensive” or every growing SME a compounder.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence comprises FY26/FY25 full annual reports and their complete statutory annexures, FY24 report for corroboration, final IPOprospectus, the May 2026 results, issuer presentations, Septemberorders/resignations/Sabveupdate, the NSEcaution and tribunal plan. Official dated exchange market/security/calendar files authenticate quote, shares, lot and session roster. The three peer annual reports are dated business-economics benchmarks, not a synthesized current peer valuation table. Exact URLs, page anchors and SHA256 payload receipts are retained in the source register; original documents are not redistributed.

Assumptions are not reported facts:15% nominal pretax equity hurdle with 12%/18% alternatives;20 October 2026–20 October 2031 horizon using actualdays/365.25; no future ordinary dividend; scenario margins/growth/WC/capex; conservative restriction of all FD; optional warrants only when modeled; unknown WCDLsplit; Sabvepayment split; collection sequencing; developer recovery haircut; terminal multiple; and hypothetical rescue price 30% belowreference with 3% fees. Rescue shares are integer-rounded, cash arrives before interval uses and ownership dilution differs from share expansion.

Open questions are specific: current renewals/cash, acquired opening balance-sheet cash classifications, customer/project remaining backlog, recoverability of aged AR/retention and developer assets, cash versus credited loan interest, actual post-approval capital calls, and full dated execution restrictions/depth. Public audited data are sufficient for a descriptive analysis but not a verified current funded investment return. The source-safe package reproduces arithmetic and model outputs from disclosed extracts; it cannot newly authenticate original PDFs that are deliberately absent. No sensitive shareholder lists, personal identifiers, raw OCR or transfer tools are included.

name: Mason Infratech Limited
summary:
Hold — unresolved funding, not “Avoid — fraud”. Mason has genuinely scaled a Mumbai-region building contractor, but the listed equity now also finances property, associates and a newly consolidated developer. FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹131.32 cr and attributable PAT ₹21.87 cr. The attractive-looking earnings multiple is not an owner-cash return: parent CFO after moving debt additions out of operating cash was −₹40.18 cr in FY26. Prior FY25 was also negative on the same economic basis. These are not explained away by the acquired subsidiary alone. [ar26; ar25]

The constructive case is tangible: owned execution equipment, repeat clients, profitable contracts, a large fresh-equity cushion and an unmodified audit with no reported lender default. The opposing case is equally tangible: capital tied in WIP, aged receivables and development investments; demand loans with interest credited rather than verified collected; and cash-credit/short-tenor facilities with dates before the investment cutoff. A positive terminal spreadsheet cannot settle those interim claims.

BQS and GQS are descriptive quality measures, not investment recommendations. GQS is capped at 5 because multi-year cash realization is persistently weak. IAS is NS rather than a fabricated low or neutral number. The ₹97 quote is authenticated on 19 October, while the analytical investment horizon is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031. Ordinary expected returns and entry prices are withheld until current financeability is demonstrated. Conditional recovery and explicit rescue branches remain useful diagnostics, not buy targets. [market60; security_master]
